# s329 — retire is a command

`slicer retire ID --reason TEXT` retires an item exactly as `slicer remove ID --reason TEXT` does.

**Findings:** outer-session wishlist 2026-10-16, item 8: reached for slicer retire, which does not exist · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**Not in this slice:** changing `remove`; an `unretire`.

## Why

On 2026-10-16 the outer session ran `slicer retire` to retire s316 and got `invalid choice`. Retiring is `remove --reason` (`src/slicer/cli.py:3724`), whose name suggests deletion, while `retired` is the status it sets and the word the docs and render use. `remove --purge` is the deleting form.
